title: SV-6: a message of no turn never holds back the CLI's own turn
head: 5c4cfa6951d69accb4c68618e75a26f46b20e16c
brief: SV-6 Claude idle reader. Between turns the idle reader (_route_idle) holds any main-thread message it cannot place; everything behind a held message is held too, including the CLI's own turn, which then waits for the owner's next send. The PR adds _of_no_turn(item), true for anything that is not a user, assistant, stream-event, result or system message (rate_limit_event, conversation_reset, any kind a newer SDK adds). Such a message is read and passed by, as a system message already is, unless it arrives behind something already held (held in order). The first held message's type is logged. Offers, adopt, self_started marking, Discord, speech, runner skips, approvals, steering and C3/C6 provenance are claimed unchanged.
focus: provenance of offered CLI turns (peer, task-notification, background)
behaviour on SDK upgrade (claude-agent-sdk is not pinned)

ground_truth.mechanism: SdkUserMessage in the _of_no_turn exclusion tuple is not pinned: removing it survives every suite, and the owner's real case (a peer-origin replay offered as 'peer', and a late steer's echo staying held/interrupted) is untested
ground_truth.evidence: mutant removing SdkUserMessage survives idle_reader_check, steer_check, claude_subagents_check, chat_relay_check; new tests use one_default whose CLI turns open with a stream event

ground_truth.mechanism: test_a_rate_limit_event_mid_cli_turn_is_read_in_order does not test order: it passes on pre-fix code and under a reorder mutant
ground_truth.evidence: reorder mutant (drop no-turn messages even behind a held one) survives; matters for ConversationResetMessage zeroing cost_seen ahead of a held result

ground_truth.mechanism: an SDK upgrade can silently widen what is dropped between turns: a new Message class is passed by with nothing logged
ground_truth.evidence: claude-agent-sdk is not declared in pyproject.toml
